I guess the investigation continues...\n" }, { "id": 258885337, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-258885337", "created_at": "2016-11-07T16:31:22Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 3", "body": "Ok, I've found some clues.\nAdding the `enable_widevine=1` flag actually made it compile the Widevine plugin components. They just weren't added to the `Chromium.app` package for some reason. The files `libwidevinecdm.dylib` and `widevinecdmadapter.plugin` are inside the `/out` folder. I tested them and they work, enabling playback on that test site as well on Netflix.\n\nHowever, a `manifest.json` file is also required for Widevine and, for some reason, it isn't being build. I discovered this by downloading Google Chrome and looking into their `.app` folder. There, I found the 2 Widevine files plus the `manifest.json`.\n\nOn OS X, you can get Widevine support on ungoogled-chromium by doing this:\n1) Create a file with the name `manifest.json` and the following contents:\n\n```\n{\n \"manifest_version\": 2,\n \"update_url\": \"https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx\",\n \"name\": \"WidevineCdm\",\n \"description\": \"Widevine Content Decryption Module\",\n \"offline_enabled\": false,\n \"version\": \"1.4.8.903\",\n \"minimum_chrome_version\": \"47.0.2526.0\",\n \"x-cdm-module-versions\": \"4\",\n \"x-cdm-interface-versions\": \"8\",\n \"x-cdm-host-versions\": \"8\",\n \"x-cdm-codecs\": \"vp8,vp9.0,avc1\",\n \"icons\": {\n \"16\": \"imgs/icon-128x128.png\",\n \"128\": \"imgs/icon-128x128.png\"\n },\n \"platforms\": [\n {\n \"os\": \"win\",\n \"arch\": \"x86\",\n \"sub_package_path\": \"_platform_specific/win_x86/\"\n },\n {\n \"os\": \"win\",\n \"arch\": \"x64\",\n \"sub_package_path\": \"_platform_specific/win_x64/\"\n },\n {\n \"os\": \"mac\",\n \"arch\": \"x86\",\n \"sub_package_path\": \"_platform_specific/mac_x86/\"\n },\n {\n \"os\": \"mac\",\n \"arch\": \"x64\",\n \"sub_package_path\": \"_platform_specific/mac_x64/\"\n }\n ]\n}\n```\n\n2) Get inside your `Chromium.app` package, and go to `Contents/Versions/your_chromium_version/Chromium Framework.framework/`\n3) Create a `Libraries` folder there\n4) Inside it, paste the `WidevineCdm`folder from the `/out` folder.\n5) Put the `manifest.json` inside the `WidevineCdm` folder.\n\nIt should work now. Alternatively, you can just download Chrome and copy the Libraries folder from their package - it also works, even if the Chromium and Chrome versions don't match.\nPutting these files inside a `Chromium.app` package that was built without the `enable_widevine=1` flag doesn't work.\n\nThe Windows/Linux builds might be getting similar behavior (`widevinecdm.dll`/`libwidevinecdm.so` files left in the out folder without being used). We probably can get Widevine support in a similar way with them.\n" }, { "id": 258932180, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-258932180", "created_at": "2016-11-07T19:11:36Z", "updated_at": "2016-11-07T19:12:35Z", "author": "Participant 2", "body": "You have `libwidevinecdm.dylib`? That's weird. We don't have the source code to that library, which means it must have downloaded while it's building. Only the widevinecdmadapter library is built.\n\nBTW, I scanned the GYP file and it seems that the manifest.json file is also provided before the build starts. So it seems we're only supposed to have the widevinecdmadapter library.\n\nEDIT: If we need to modify any meta-build configuration files, I would like to wait until we've switched to GN first.\n" }, { "id": 258939147, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-258939147", "created_at": "2016-11-07T19:37:07Z", "updated_at": "2016-11-07T20:05:22Z", "author": "Participant 3", "body": "Yes, I have `libwidevinecdm.dylib`. Though I will try to squeeze in time this weekend to update the necessary patches to GN.\n" }, { "id": 258990474, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-258990474", "created_at": "2016-11-07T22:56:44Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 3", "body": "Okay.\nAny clues on why those 2 files are not being moved to the `Chromium.app` package?\n" }, { "id": 258997630, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-258997630", "created_at": "2016-11-07T23:30:43Z", "updated_at": "2016-11-07T23:31:25Z", "author": "Participant 2", "body": "Not exactly sure yet since the packaging method is unique on Mac, but it's more than likely related to the differences in behavior when using Chromium instead of Chrome for branding.\n" }, { "id": 259906525, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-259906525", "created_at": "2016-11-11T08:28:30Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 11", "body": "![chrome_2016-11-11_02-27-27](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4476501/20208868/7c5cf5f4-a7b6-11e6-8b72-b5bdcc31f4eb.png)\n\nWindows 7 user, latest release. Its smaller than the one Chrome provides (1.4MB vs 5.2MB)\r\n\r\nReplacing it with Google Chrome's `libwidevinecdm.dylib` fixes the problem." }, { "id": 267435428, "url": "https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-267435428", "created_at": "2016-12-15T20:29:25Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 2", "body": "@gcarq Thanks for your input. [altblitz got Widevine to work just fine on Linux](https://github.com/Eloston/ungoogled-chromium/issues/73#issuecomment-252962092) doing exactly what you said.\r\n\r\n@9Morello On Linux, a stub version of `libwidevinecdm.so` is built. I'm assuming Windows and macOS have the same behavior (but have their respective file names). It's not broken, it's just a dummy placeholder. You will always need to get the official library from Chrome, unless they miraculously release the source code.
